#table(stroke: none, columns: 2, align: (center, center, ), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 0), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 1), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 2), table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [$t$ (days)], [$W(t)$ $lr((""^(degree) upright(C)))$], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [0], [20], [3], [31], [6], [28], [9], [24], [12], [22], [15], [21], table.hline(stroke: .5pt));

The temperature, in degrees Celsius ( $""^(degree) upright(C)$ ), of the water in a pond is a differentiable function $W$ of time $t$. The table above shows the water temperature as recorded every 3 days over a 15-day period.

(a) Use data from the table to find an approximation for $W'(12)$. Show the computations that lead to your answer. Indicate units of measure.

(b) Approximate the average temperature, in degrees Celsius, of the water over the time interval $0 <= t <= 15$ days by using a trapezoidal approximation with subintervals of length $Delta t = 3$ days.

(c) A student proposes the function $P$, given by $P(t)= 20 + 10 t e^((- t \/ 3))$, as a model for the temperature of the water in the pond at time $t$, where $t$ is measured in days and $P(t)$ is measured in degrees Celsius. Find $P'(12)$. Using appropriate units, explain the meaning of your answer in terms of water temperature.

(d) Use the function $P$ defined in part (c) to find the average value, in degrees Celsius, of $P(t)$ over the time interval $0 <= t <= 15$ days.
